transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Maya Cheng (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood), Carlos Mendez (SummitCloud Head of Partnerships), Aisha Rahman (PM), Tomoko Saito (Platform Architect), Ben Li (Security)
Links referenced: Redwood deck - marketplace-packaging (redwood.ai/decks/marketplace-packaging), sample AMI script (to be shared), SummitCloud procurement flow (customer doc)

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: packaging options for marketplace listing, reference arch for hybrid / managed instances, and security + procurement notes. we wanted to get aligned on what SummitCloud needs to present this in your marketplace catalog.

00:18 Carlos: hey thanks Maya, yeah two quick priorities for us — we need a clean story for ops teams about how the product will be deployed (AMI or SaaS), and also a clear billing/procurement flow so we can map to our marketplace checkout. timeline — we want a soft listing by early jan if possible.

00:36 Maya: great, that timeline is feasible, depending on the packaging path. we'll run through three recommended paths: 1) Hosted Redwood API (SaaS listing) — fastest time to market; 2) Marketplace image / AMI that customers can launch into their account (good for VPC isolation); 3) Private managed deployment that SummitCloud can offer as a managed service for regulated customers.

00:58 Aisha: can you clarify differences on the ops side? like what does SummitCloud have to manage for AMI vs hosted?

01:10 Liam: yeah big picture — AMI: you supply an image we produce which includes the inference runtime and a small bootstrap that talks to the customer's KMS and our license server. Customer manages the infra, scaling, updates. For SaaS listing, Redwood hosts the inference and handles scaling; SummitCloud handles identity and billing via marketplace seat/subscription. For private managed, it's more of a joint runbook — we can run in your VPC or co-managed cluster.

01:40 Tomoko: for AMI customers we have strict CIDR policies and NAT requirements; we can't open wide egress. what are your outbound dependencies?

01:52 Priya: runtime has two outbound touchpoints on AMI: license/heartbeat to Redwood control plane (optional for air-gapped) and container image updates. both can be proxied through customer egress; we can also produce an offline bundle if needed. note: the KV cache telemetry and usage metrics are opt-in.

02:12 Ben: we need the KMS story — customers will want to use their own KMS, not Redwood's. can the AMI accept customer-managed KMS?

02:24 Liam: yes, we support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping. in AMI flow we read a KMS endpoint configured at bootstrap; for SaaS we integrate with customer KMS via bring-your-own-key (BYOK) federations or via customer-managed HSM in private deployments.

02:46 Carlos: procurement question — if we list as AMI in marketplace, how does billing flow? do you want us to charge seats or is it a marketplace metered billing?

03:00 Maya: good question. three billing patterns: 1) Marketplace metered — marketplace takes percent and forwards usage to Redwood; 2) Subscription seat — SummitCloud sells a managed offering and pays Redwood a committed reserved capacity fee; 3) Marketplace referral — less common. We'll share a short matrix in the checklist.

03:25 Aisha: okay can you add the downstream billing flow diagram for metered usage? we need that for legal.

03:37 Maya: yes, we'll include a sample flow and a template contract snippet.

03:45 Tomoko: networking — regarding VPC peering: we prefer customers keep everything in their VPC and avoid peering unless necessary. does Redwood require peering for low latency inference?

03:58 Liam: not strictly; for AMI deployments there is no peering requirement. For private managed (we run in your VPC) we use VPC endpoints and can avoid full peering. For dedicated capacity in our cloud, we do cross-region routing but that's a hosted model. we will document recommended NAT and endpoint configs.

04:24 Ben: audit log requirements — can you provide sample audit logs and retention options? we need to map to our SIEM ingest pipeline.

04:36 Priya: yes we can produce structured audit logs (JSON) with token-level event types. retention is configurable; we can push to customer S3 or a syslog endpoint. expect small differences in field names in the exported logs — little things like KV cache is sometimes transcribed as K-V cash :)

04:58 Carlos: haha noted. on certification: are you SOC2 compliant today? customer legal will ask.

05:06 Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II. we'll attach redacted report and SOC2 scope. we'll also include our penetration test summary.

05:18 Aisha: for the joint solution page we need a reference architecture diagram. can you walk through your recommended flow for a hybrid customer who wants low latency, KMS-owned keys, and local model hosting?

05:34 Liam: sure — recommended pattern is: customer hosts model runtime in their VPC via the marketplace AMI (or GCP image). They configure KMS for key wrapping, enable a private endpoint to receive model weights from an internal artifact store. Redwood provides a control plane agent (lightweight) that handles license validation and metrics — this can operate over a proxied outbound only, or be disabled for air-gapped installs. For latency-sensitive endpoints, enable local batching and set sequence length defaults; we'll provide recommended instance types and GPU profiles in the doc.

06:12 Tomoko: instance sizing — do you have per-model recommended instance types? our customers often ask about T4 vs A10 vs A100 equivalents on each cloud.

06:22 Priya: yes, we'll provide a model-profile matrix. for example: 7B family -> 1xA10 or 2xT4 depending on throughput; 70B -> A100 or high memory instances. we'll share the latest profile sheet. the runtime supports quantized kernels which can run on cheaper SKUs but with caveats.

06:45 Carlos: any special kernel dependencies? some of our customers are locked to certain AMIs.

06:52 Liam: the AMI includes CUDA 11.x and a pinned libc; we document the kernel drivers and AMI baselines. if customers have strict locked images we can provide a containerized bundle rather than a full AMI, but disk image methods have tradeoffs.

07:12 Aisha: security review — Ben wants to know about RBAC for operators and audit surfaces.

07:20 Ben: yes, RBAC, role separation, SSO — SAML or OIDC?

07:26 Maya: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for account-level RBAC. The AMI agent has an operator RBAC model that can be integrated with customer IAM roles; logs are exported for audit.

07:42 Ben: what about database persistence — where do you keep model metadata if we run AMI?

07:48 Priya: metadata is stored either locally in a small SQLite instance encrypted at rest, or optionally forwarded to the customer's managed database. we can also send metadata to your S3 bucket if preferred.

08:00 Tomoko: for the marketplace listing we need marketing assets: screenshots, architecture diagram, short 60s video. can Redwood provide those or do we need to make them?

08:12 Maya: we'll provide a starter kit: logos, two diagrams (SaaS and AMI), a short product demo clip, and a one-page capability matrix. we'll attach in the checklist.

08:26 Carlos: procurement/legal — time to complete legal review for marketplace is usually 3 weeks on our side. can we push a launcher plan into december?

08:35 Maya: yes if we get the security docs and packaging checklist this week, we can aim for an internal SummitCloud readiness review in early december and a soft listing in mid-jan.

08:46 Liam: a few gotchas to call out: 1) offline/air-gapped customers require a separate distribution flow; 2) telemetry off by default for regulated installs; 3) some kernels may need libary patches on older instances — we'll note that in the AMI notes.

09:05 Aisha: for the POC runbook — can you outline quick perf steps (latency p95, throughput, token cost)? we want to run a short validation in our staging lane.

09:18 Liam: we'll send a perf runbook: suggested datasets, prompt shapes, warmup steps for KV cache, and a small harness script. expected outputs: p95 latency numbers, tokens/sec, and guidance on batching settings. we'll also include a small benchmark spreadsheet.

09:38 Ben: just to confirm: for keys — the customer-managed KMS integration means the private key never leaves the customer KMS, correct?

09:45 Priya: correct. we perform key wrapping and the private key remains with customer KMS. we only hold wrapped keys or license tokens.

09:56 Carlos: any competitors doing this differently? we had flagged CloudWave as doing marketplace AMIs but with more limited telemetry.

10:05 Maya: yep CloudWave does a simpler AMI but fewer operational features. NimbusCloud has a more managed experience but higher cost. we'll include a short competitor notes blob.

10:18 Tomoko: follow up — can you encode a CIDR pre-check script? some of our customers get tripped up on overlapping CIDRs during peering.

10:28 Liam: yes, we'll include a small python script and a checklist for CIDR and route table requirements.

10:40 Maya: ok let's recap next steps — I'll share the marketplace packaging checklist and AMI sample. Liam will produce networking and VPC peering doc plus perf runbook. Tomoko and Ben will provide staging details and security policy. we'll reconvene after the infra deep dive.

10:58 Carlos: perfect, thanks everyone. that was helpful.

11:03 Maya: thanks all — we'll get notes and artifacts over by Friday. bye.

[transcription notes: occasional mis-heard terms (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache); timestamps approximate at 30-90s intervals; speaker attribution mostly accurate but some overlaps were condensed. shared artifacts to be attached to follow-up email.]
